## Uses in popular culture

[[edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Message_(Grandmaster_Flash_and_the_Furious_Five_song)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section's source code: Uses in popular culture")]

The rhythm track has been [sampled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sampling_(music) "Sampling (music)") in various hip hop songs, including [Sinbad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinbad_(entertainer) "Sinbad (entertainer)")'s 1990 comedy song "Brain Damaged", the remix for the 1993 song "[Check Yo Self](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Check_Yo_Self "Check Yo Self")" by [Ice Cube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_Cube "Ice Cube"),[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Message_(Grandmaster_Flash_and_the_Furious_Five_song)#cite_note-31) the 1997 song "[Can't Nobody Hold Me Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Nobody_Hold_Me_Down "Can't Nobody Hold Me Down")" by [Puff Daddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puff_Daddy "Puff Daddy"),[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Message_(Grandmaster_Flash_and_the_Furious_Five_song)#cite_note-32) the 2011 song "Teen Pregnancy" by [Blank Banshee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blank_Banshee "Blank Banshee"), and the 2022 song "[Players](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Players_(Coi_Leray_song) "Players (Coi Leray song)")" by [Coi Leray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coi_Leray "Coi Leray").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Message_(Grandmaster_Flash_and_the_Furious_Five_song)#cite_note-33)

On the DVD _The [Genesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genesis\_(band) "Genesis (band)") Songbook_, the band and producer [Hugh Padgham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Padgham "Hugh Padgham") revealed that the inspiration for [Phil Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Collins "Phil Collins")' menacing laugh on their 1983 song "[Mama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama_(Genesis_song) "Mama (Genesis song)")" came from "The Message".

The refrain beginning with "Don't push me 'cuz I'm close to the edge" was referenced in the animated movie _[Happy Feet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy\_Feet "Happy Feet")_.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Message_(Grandmaster_Flash_and_the_Furious_Five_song)#cite_note-34)

A line from the song was sampled in "Movement in Still Life" by [BT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BT_(musician) "BT (musician)"), the title track from his 1999 album _[Movement in Still Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Movement\_in\_Still\_Life "Movement in Still Life")_.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Message_(Grandmaster_Flash_and_the_Furious_Five_song)#cite_note-35)

In 2005, a mural inspired by "The Message" was painted in the [Newtown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newtown,_New_South_Wales "Newtown, New South Wales") neighbourhood of [Sydney, Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney,_Australia "Sydney, Australia") by artist Colin Bebe. "It's Like a Jungle Sometimes" depicts the streets of Newtown as a literal jungle, with animals roaming the streets and swinging from poles, as a commentary on the artist's mental health and struggle with suicideality. In September 2017, [street art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street_art "Street art")-based [advertising agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advertising_agency "Advertising agency") Apparition Media painted over it with a mural promoting the film _[Mother!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mother! "Mother!")_, featuring a giant portrait of [Jennifer Lawrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Lawrence "Jennifer Lawrence") and the caption "#mothermovie."[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Message_(Grandmaster_Flash_and_the_Furious_Five_song)#cite_note-36) Much public outrage followed, as the mural had become much-loved in the community. Within hours, it had been graffitied by someone who added: "Fuck off! It really is a jungle sometimes. No respect!"[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Message_(Grandmaster_Flash_and_the_Furious_Five_song)#cite_note-37) Apparition Media apologised and word of the incident also reached _Mother!'_ s director, [Darren Aronofsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darren_Aronofsky "Darren Aronofsky"), who tweeted that he was "embarrassed and furious" and would pay for the mural to be restored. It was restored in December 2017.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Message_(Grandmaster_Flash_and_the_Furious_Five_song)#cite_note-38)

A reference to the lyrics was included in the song Cabinet Battle #1 from the 2015 musical [_Hamilton_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamilton_(musical) "Hamilton (musical)").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Message_(Grandmaster_Flash_and_the_Furious_Five_song)#cite_note-39)

In 2007, the 25th anniversary of "The Message", [Melle Mel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melle_Mel "Melle Mel") changed the spelling of his first name to Mele Mel and released "M3 - The New Message" as the first single to his first ever solo album, _Muscles_. 2007 was also the year that Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five became the first [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop_music "Hip hop music") act ever to be inducted into the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Message_(Grandmaster_Flash_and_the_Furious_Five_song)#cite_note-40)

A Swedish translation/adaptation of the song, "Budskapet", was released by [Timbuktu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timbuktu_(artist) "Timbuktu (artist)") in May 2013, following the [riots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_2013_Stockholm_riots "May 2013 Stockholm riots") in [Husby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Husby,_Stockholm "Husby, Stockholm") and other suburbs of Stockholm.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Message_(Grandmaster_Flash_and_the_Furious_Five_song)#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Message_(Grandmaster_Flash_and_the_Furious_Five_song)#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Message_(Grandmaster_Flash_and_the_Furious_Five_song)#cite_note-43)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame

The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, established in 1983 and located in Cleveland, Ohio, United States, is dedicated to recording the history of some of the best-known and most influential musicians, bands, producers, and others that have in some major way influenced the music industry, particularly in the area of rock and roll.[1] Originally, there were four categories of induction: performers, non-performers, early influences, and lifetime achievement. In 2000, sidemen was introduced as a category, which has since been altered to musical excellence.

The only category that has seen new inductees every single year is the performers category. Artists become eligible for induction in that category 25 years after the release of their first record.[2] In order to be inducted, an artist must be nominated by a committee that selects a number of candidates. Ballots are then sent to more than 1,000 "rock experts" who evaluate the candidates and vote on who should be inducted. The performers that receive the highest number of votes are inducted. This number varies; for example, seven were inducted in 2019. Starting in 2012, fans could vote on a fan ballot with an equal weight to the other ballots.[2] New inductees are honored at an annual ceremony held at the Hall of Fame in Cleveland every even-numbered year and either New York City or Los Angeles every odd-numbered year.[3]

The three other categories are selected by committees instead of the annual ballot.[4] In 2025, Rock Hall chairman John Sykes said, "No matter what category you're in, Performer or those other three, it's the same size plaque on the wall right next to Bob Dylan, Aretha Franklin, and the Beatles. It's not a secondary award. It's equal to getting in as a performer."[4]

Musical influenceedit

This category recognizes artists whose music and performance style influenced the evolution of rock and roll. Originally honoring "Early" artists who predated the birth of rock & roll, the category celebrates those with a profound impact on music who inspired rock's leading artists.[2] Inductees are selected by a committee.[2] Since 2023,[181] the "Early Influence" award has been named "Musical Influence".

Singlesedit

At the 2018 ceremony, a new induction category for singles was announced by Steven Van Zandt.[259] According to Van Zandt, the category is "a recognition of the excellence of the singles that shaped rock 'n' roll, kind of a rock 'n' roll jukebox, records by artists not in the Rock Hall – which is not to say these artists will never be in the Rock Hall. They just are not in the Rock Hall at the moment."[259] However, The Isley Brothers, whose song "Twist and Shout" was inducted in 2019, were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as performers in 1992. Link Wray and Chubby Checker, whose songs were honored in this category, were later inducted into the Hall: Wray in 2023 through the Musical Influence category, and Checker in 2025 in the main Performers category.

Individuals inducted twice or moreedit

As of 2026, twenty-nine performers have been inducted twice or more; sixteen have been recognized as a solo artist and with a duo or group, and eleven have been inducted with two separate groups.[263] Eric Clapton is the only person to be inducted three times: as a solo artist, with Cream, and with the Yardbirds.[264] Clyde McPhatter was the first to ever be inducted twice and is one of three artists to be inducted first as a solo artist and then as a member of a group, the other artists being Neil Young and Rod Stewart. Stephen Stills is the only artist to be inducted twice in the same year.

Crosby, Stills & Nash and the Beatles are the only two bands whose members were also each inducted separately, with other acts or as solo artists. In addition to their 1997 induction with CSN, David Crosby was inducted with the Byrds in 1991, Stephen Stills with Buffalo Springfield in 1997, and Graham Nash with the Hollies in 2010. After their 1988 induction with the Beatles, John Lennon, Paul McCartney, and George Harrison were inducted as solo artists in the main performer category in 1994, 1999, and 2004, respectively, while Ringo Starr was inducted in the Award for Musical Excellence category in 2015.

There are several performers who were inducted with one (or more) of the bands they played for, but were not inducted as members of one (or more) other bands. For example, Neil Young was inducted with Buffalo Springfield and as a solo artist, but was left out when Crosby, Stills & Nash were inducted.

In 2019, Stevie Nicks became the first woman to be inducted twice, after having been inducted with Fleetwood Mac in 1998.[265] She was later joined by Carole King and Tina Turner. In 2021, Carole King was the first person to be inducted as both a performer and a non-performer.

John Lennon and Dave Grohl are the only two multiple inductees who were inducted in their first year of eligibility on both inductions.

and explicitly mark omissions. A partial, restricted or truncated list is not the
complete candidate set. Missing fields are unknown. Keep relevant discoveries even
if they answer a different part of the original question.

paths on an observed site are allowed. Child notes are returned automatically;

when expansion stops.

The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame

The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, established in 1983 and located in Cleveland, Ohio, United States, is dedicated to recording the history of some of the best-known and most influential musicians, bands, producers, and others that have in some major way influenced the music industry, particularly in the area of rock and roll.[1] Originally, there were four categories of induction: performers, non-performers, early influences, and lifetime achievement. In 2000, sidemen was introduced as a category, which has since been altered to musical excellence.

The only category that has seen new inductees every single year is the performers category. Artists become eligible for induction in that category 25 years after the release of their first record.[2] In order to be inducted, an artist must be nominated by a committee that selects a number of candidates. Ballots are then sent to more than 1,000 "rock experts" who evaluate the candidates and vote on who should be inducted. The performers that receive the highest number of votes are inducted. This number varies; for example, seven were inducted in 2019. Starting in 2012, fans could vote on a fan ballot with an equal weight to the other ballots.[2] New inductees are honored at an annual ceremony held at the Hall of Fame in Cleveland every even-numbered year and either New York City or Los Angeles every odd-numbered year.[3]

The three other categories are selected by committees instead of the annual ballot.[4] In 2025, Rock Hall chairman John Sykes said, "No matter what category you're in, Performer or those other three, it's the same size plaque on the wall right next to Bob Dylan, Aretha Franklin, and the Beatles. It's not a secondary award. It's equal to getting in as a performer."[4]

Musical influenceedit

This category recognizes artists whose music and performance style influenced the evolution of rock and roll. Originally honoring "Early" artists who predated the birth of rock & roll, the category celebrates those with a profound impact on music who inspired rock's leading artists.[2] Inductees are selected by a committee.[2] Since 2023,[181] the "Early Influence" award has been named "Musical Influence".

Non-performers (Ahmet Ertegun Award)edit

The non-performer category honors "songwriters, producers, disc jockeys, record executives, journalists and other industry professionals who have had a major influence on the development of rock and roll".[2] Several of the inductees in this category were in fact prominent performers as well. The inductees in this category are selected by the same committee that chooses the early influences.[2] In 2008, this category was renamed the "Ahmet Ertegun Award".[232]

Award for Musical Excellenceedit

Established in 2000 as "Sidemen", the category "honors those musicians, producers and others who have spent their careers out of the spotlight working with major artists on various parts of their recording and live careers". Singlesedit

At the 2018 ceremony, a new induction category for singles was announced by Steven Van Zandt.[259] According to Van Zandt, the category is "a recognition of the excellence of the singles that shaped rock 'n' roll, kind of a rock 'n' roll jukebox, records by artists not in the Rock Hall – which is not to say these artists will never be in the Rock Hall. They just are not in the Rock Hall at the moment."[259] However, The Isley Brothers, whose song "Twist and Shout" was inducted in 2019, were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as performers in 1992. Link Wray and Chubby Checker, whose songs were honored in this category, were later inducted into the Hall: Wray in 2023 through the Musical Influence category, and Checker in 2025 in the main Performers category.

Individuals inducted twice or moreedit

As of 2026, twenty-nine performers have been inducted twice or more; sixteen have been recognized as a solo artist and with a duo or group, and eleven have been inducted with two separate groups.[263] Eric Clapton is the only person to be inducted three times: as a solo artist, with Cream, and with the Yardbirds.[264] Clyde McPhatter was the first to ever be inducted twice and is one of three artists to be inducted first as a solo artist and then as a member of a group, the other artists being Neil Young and Rod Stewart. Stephen Stills is the only artist to be inducted twice in the same year.

Crosby, Stills & Nash and the Beatles are the only two bands whose members were also each inducted separately, with other acts or as solo artists. In addition to their 1997 induction with CSN, David Crosby was inducted with the Byrds in 1991, Stephen Stills with Buffalo Springfield in 1997, and Graham Nash with the Hollies in 2010. After their 1988 induction with the Beatles, John Lennon, Paul McCartney, and George Harrison were inducted as solo artists in the main performer category in 1994, 1999, and 2004, respectively, while Ringo Starr was inducted in the Award for Musical Excellence category in 2015.

There are several performers who were inducted with one (or more) of the bands they played for, but were not inducted as members of one (or more) other bands. For example, Neil Young was inducted with Buffalo Springfield and as a solo artist, but was left out when Crosby, Stills & Nash were inducted.

In 2019, Stevie Nicks became the first woman to be inducted twice, after having been inducted with Fleetwood Mac in 1998.[265] She was later joined by Carole King and Tina Turner. In 2021, Carole King was the first person to be inducted as both a performer and a non-performer.

John Lennon and Dave Grohl are the only two multiple inductees who were inducted in their first year of eligibility on both inductions.

**2007 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductees with the longest‑charting Hot 100 single (prior to January 2024)**  

| Artist | Song | Weeks on Billboard Hot 100 (short‑term peak 1991–84) |
|--------|------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| **R.E.M.** | *Losing My Religion* | 21 weeks |
| **Van Halen** | *Jump* | 21 weeks |

*Both songs tied for the most weeks on the Billboard Hot 100 among the five 2007 inductees.*  
- R.E.M.’s *Losing My Religion* (1991) peaked at #4 and remained on the chart for 21 weeks.  
- Van Halen’s *Jump* (1984) peaked at #1 and also logged 21 weeks on the Hot 100.  

These are the only 2007 inductees whose singles reached more than a dozen weeks on the chart, giving them the longest‑charting entries of that class.
